facts.claim: In real-life conflicts recorded by cameras, bystanders were 19 times more likely to intervene when danger was present than when it was not.
facts.quote: In the presence of danger, bystanders were 19 times more likely to intervene than in the absence of danger.

facts.claim: The bystander effect was attenuated when situations were perceived as dangerous, perpetrators were present, and the costs of intervention were physical.
facts.quote: The bystander effect was attenuated when situations were perceived as dangerous (compared with non-dangerous), perpetrators were present (compared with non-present), and the costs of intervention were physical (compared with non-physical).

facts.claim: The presence of other people in a critical situation reduces the likelihood that an individual will help.
facts.quote: Research on bystander intervention has produced a great number of studies showing that the presence of other people in a critical situation reduces the likelihood that an individual will help.

facts.claim: School-based programs increased bystander intervention both on a practical and statistically significant level.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, this meta-analysis indicated that programs increased bystander intervention both on a practical and statistically significant level.

facts.claim: Bystander naloxone administration and overdose education programs are associated with increased odds of recovery.
facts.quote: Empirical evidence in the research literature suggests that bystander naloxone administration and overdose education programs are associated with increased odds of recovery

facts.claim: Bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation increases the survival of out-of-hospital cardiac arrests.
facts.quote: Based on currently available evidence, the findings of this meta-analysis suggest that BCPR increases the survival of OHCAs

research.angle: While the presence of others generally reduces the likelihood of helping, real-life footage shows that the presence of danger significantly increases the likelihood of bystander intervention.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that while the 'bystander effect' exists, it is significantly mitigated by the presence of danger and specific situational factors.
research.caveat: The finding that danger increases intervention is based on a specific analysis of 80 interpersonal conflicts recorded by public surveillance cameras.
